capabilities: Upload pasted or dropped images and replace placeholders with remote links
Upload to GitHub via the Contents API with branches and date paths
Upload to a generic image host via POST multipart/form-data
Build CDN or proxy URLs from a base directory (GitHub Raw, jsDelivr, Statically)
Restore the local image link when an upload fails
extras: The README warns that the GitHub token is stored as plain text in data.json and advises a least-privilege, revocable token; it also notes that Raw and public CDN links cannot read private repositories anonymously.
intentEvidence: Pastepic is an independently implemented MIT-licensed project.
motivation: The author built it to keep one paste-to-upload image workflow across desktop, tablet, and mobile Obsidian, since existing workflows were desktop-oriented.
problem: Manually opening an image host, uploading, copying a URL, and pasting it back breaks the writing flow, and local images make the vault grow quickly.

relations.evidence: image-paste events, uploader abstraction, and failure fallback
GitHub Contents API, multi-host settings, and CDN URL organization
paste placeholders, drag-and-drop uploads, and image-host workflows

summary: Uploads pasted, dropped, or newly inserted images to GitHub or a custom image host and replaces them with remote Markdown CDN links.
